question: How is one situated among the yogini group designated within the Kula tradition?
premises: A person is situated in the middle of the yogini group
That person is identified as an animal
This designation is stated in the Kula
inference: In the Kula tradition, one placed among the yogini group is called a paśu
uncertainties: Whether paśu here means sacrificial victim or bound being
plain_english: In the Kula, he who is situated in the midst of the group of yoginis is called a paśu.
